newsitem.title: USA: Lifecore sees benefit from lease buyout.
newsitem.headline: Lifecore sees benefit from lease buyout.

text.p: Lifecore Biomedical Inc said it expects its operating costs to be reduced by its completion of an accelerated early buyout of its lease with Johnson & Johnson.

Under the terms of a $7.9-million equipment lease started in May 1991, the first eligible buyout period was to occur in November 1997, with the buyout consisting of a $5.4 million payment. The companies agreed to an accelerated schedule "to facilitate Lifecore's expansion of its current manufacturing operations," it said.
"The lease termination is expected to favorably impact ongoing financial operating costs," Lifecore said.
The debt reduction accomplished by the lease termination was part of planned uses of proceeds discussed in Lifecore's 1995 and 1996 equity financings.
Lifecore makes medical and surgical devices for use in dentistry, ophthalmology, veterinary, and wound care.
